name: Efpeglenatide
route: Weekly injection under the skin (in trials)
status: Investigational, not FDA-approved: phase 3 trials in obesity (completed) and type 2 diabetes (recruiting)
mechanism: Exendin-4 based GLP-1 drug attached to an antibody fragment so it lasts a week, raising insulin when glucose is high and easing appetite
uses: Lowering heart and kidney event risk (studied)

article.summary: Efpeglenatide is a once-weekly GLP-1 drug still in development for obesity and type 2 diabetes. A large trial showed fewer cardiovascular events, but it is not FDA-approved.
article.takeaway: Efpeglenatide is an investigational once-weekly GLP-1 drug that links an exendin-4 based peptide to an antibody fragment. In the AMPLITUDE-O trial of 4,076 people with type 2 diabetes and heart or kidney risk, it cut major cardiovascular events by about a quarter compared with placebo.[^1] A shorter obesity study in people without diabetes also showed more weight loss than placebo.[^2] Sanofi listed several of its phase 3 diabetes trials as terminated, and the Korean developer Hanmi is now running its own phase 3 program.[^3][^4][^5]
glance: Investigational; Hanmi phase 3 trials in obesity (completed) and type 2 diabetes (recruiting)[^4][^5]
Type 2 diabetes, obesity, heart and kidney risk
Weekly injection under the skin in trials
AMPLITUDE-O (4,076 people) plus smaller phase 2 and phase 3 studies

blocks.text: GLP-1 is a gut hormone released after meals. It prompts the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar is high, slows stomach emptying and signals fullness to the brain. Natural GLP-1 is broken down within minutes.

Efpeglenatide is built on exendin-4, the GLP-1 mimic used in [exenatide](/peptides/exenatide), and is joined to a piece of a human antibody (an Fc fragment) that slows its clearance, so one injection a week is enough.

Hanmi Pharmaceutical developed the drug under the code HM11260C, and it is described as under development for obesity.[^6] Sanofi ran the AMPLITUDE phase 3 diabetes program, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists several of those trials, such as the comparison with dulaglutide, as terminated.[^3]
Hanmi's own phase 3 trial in adults with obesity and no diabetes is listed as completed, and a phase 3 trial in type 2 diabetes added to metformin and dapagliflozin is recruiting.[^4][^5]

rows: 4,076 adults with type 2 diabetes and heart or kidney disease
Major cardiovascular events in 7.0% vs 9.2% on placebo (hazard ratio 0.73)[^1]
Kidney composite events in 13.0% vs 18.4% on placebo (hazard ratio 0.68)[^1]
Adults with obesity or overweight, no diabetes, 20 weeks
More weight loss than placebo at every dose tested[^2]

blocks.text: Major cardiovascular events here means heart attack, stroke, or death from cardiovascular or unknown causes. The results come from different populations and cannot be compared directly with semaglutide or tirzepatide trials.

items: **Common:** diarrhea, constipation, nausea, vomiting and bloating were more frequent than with placebo[^1]
**Follow-up:** AMPLITUDE-O followed people for a median of 1.8 years, so long-term safety is not established[^1]
**Class concerns:** approved GLP-1 drugs carry warnings about thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents, pancreatitis and gallbladder problems; efpeglenatide has no label because it is unapproved

blocks.text: What happens next depends on the Hanmi phase 3 results and on whether the company files for approval. Neither had been confirmed in the sources checked for this entry.

evidence.label: Promising, but development is uncertain
evidence.text: AMPLITUDE-O is a large randomized trial with hard outcomes, but it covered people with type 2 diabetes and a short follow-up.[^1] Evidence in obesity rests on smaller, shorter studies.[^2]

faq.a: No. It is investigational and not FDA-approved. [Semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide) and [dulaglutide](/peptides/dulaglutide) are approved weekly GLP-1 drugs.

faq.q: Did it reduce heart attacks and strokes?
faq.a: In AMPLITUDE-O it lowered a composite of heart attack, stroke and death from cardiovascular or unknown causes (hazard ratio 0.73), but only in people with type 2 diabetes and existing risk.[^1]

faq.q: How is it different from exenatide?
faq.a: Both are based on exendin-4. Efpeglenatide adds an antibody fragment to extend its action to a week. See [exenatide](/peptides/exenatide) for the approved drug.
